summary:
Over the past 25 years, NASA has monitored planetary fire activity using two distinct satellite sensor families: MODIS (1,000m) on Terra/Aqua and VIIRS (375m) on Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20. Because VIIRS provides nearly 7x higher spatial detail, raw active fire records exhibit an artificial +285% step-jump in 2012, creating a false visual impression that planetary fires tripled overnight. 

AegisFire solves this calibration break by leveraging the 13-year concurrent observation window (2012–2025). Utilizing Uber H3 hexagonal discrete global tessellation (3.5km) to eliminate spatial distortion, AegisFire trains a HistGradientBoosting cross-sensor regressor (R² = 0.8801) that translates historical MODIS metrics into VIIRS-equivalent Fire Radiative Power (FRP) with dual quantile uncertainty bounds. AegisFire delivers the first continuous 26-year Burning Activity Calendar, restoring unbroken climate intelligence.
details:
# AegisFire: Continuous Multi-Decadal Sensor Harmonization Engine

### 1. What does it do and how does it work?

AegisFire bridges 26 years of disparate orbital satellite records from NASA FIRMS: MODIS (1,000m on Terra/Aqua, active 2000–2025) and VIIRS (375m on Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20, active 2012–2025). Uncalibrated active fire time series exhibit an artificial +285% step-jump in 2012 caused solely by sensor resolution differences.

AegisFire solves this through a three-stage mathematical pipeline:

1. Discrete Hexagonal Spatial Discretization (Uber H3 at 3.5km resolution): Standardizes disparate point detections into uniform hexagonal metric cells, eliminating the 1.414x diagonal distortion of standard rectangular lat/long grids.

2. Cross-Sensor Machine Learning Transfer: Harnesses over 5,500 co-located burning cells during the 2012–2025 overlap period. Trains an ensemble HistGradientBoosting Regressor mapping MODIS FRP, scan zenith angle, and brightness temperature to true VIIRS 375m equivalent energy with an R² score of 0.8801.

3. Quantile Uncertainty Envelopes: Dual quantile regressors (q=0.10, q=0.90) provide rigorous 90% confidence intervals.

4. Optical Bowtie De-Warper: Mathematically inverts the 9.6 km² pixel footprint ballooning at extreme satellite scan angles (55° zenith).

### 2. Intended Impact & Benefits

- Eliminates the 2012 calibration break, providing climate scientists with the first uncorrupted 26-year continuous active fire baseline.

- Interactive Burning Activity Calendar: A 52-week by 26-year matrix (1,352 weekly cells) tracking dynamic climate anomaly Z-scores to reveal shifting fire seasons.

- Tactical Decision Support: Automatically generates NWCG ICS-209 incident command status reports and NASA EOSDIS CF-1.8 NetCDF-4 schemas for IPCC climate integration.

### 3. Tools, Coding Languages & Hardware

- Backend: Python 3.13, FastAPI, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn (HistGradientBoostingRegressor).

- Frontend: High-performance Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, Web Audio API (Flame Harmonic Sonification), Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons.

- Geospatial Standard: Uber H3 hexagonal discrete global grid (Resolution 7, 3.5km).
